key_insight: MedPsy’s compact medical language models combine strong benchmark performance with shorter responses, supporting more efficient edge-device deployment.
clinical_relevance: Local deployment could support privacy-sensitive medical language tasks, but these benchmark results do not establish clinical safety or patient benefit.
method: Train 1.7B and 4B text-only models using synthetic medical data and reasoning targets from a 235B teacher.
Apply two supervised fine-tuning stages, then two reinforcement-learning stages with hard-sample mining.
Evaluate GGUF quantization and real-device inference on laptop and smartphone hardware.
evidence_signal: Across seven closed-ended medical benchmarks, MedPsy-4B matched MedGemma-27B; it also scored 15.33 points higher on HealthBench-Hard and achieved 75% lower median latency and estimated energy per answer than its Qwen3 backbone at matched quantization.
watch_item: The abstract reports benchmark and device testing, not prospective clinical validation; real-world reliability requires further evaluation.
paper_title: MedPsy: State-of-the-Art Small Medical Language Models for Efficient Edge Deployment
